A: The instructional artifact is truncated to one fact and omits key terms, scenario, questions, keys, citations, and explanations.
There is no scenario and therefore no usable disciplinary decision.
B: Invented named examples and scenario details—rib cage, heart and lungs, femur, joints, torso, ribs, and shoulders—are absent from the supplied claims.
The unsupported claim that cartilage is flexible rather than hard, dense tissue is introduced as instruction and used to determine the first answer.

decisions.rationale: B is the relative winner because it supplies a usable scenario, comprehensive source claims, assessments, and instructional feedback, whereas A is effectively incomplete. B remains low quality on source fidelity because it repeatedly introduces outside anatomical details and uses an unsupported cartilage property in an assessment.
